summary: Echoes of the Cosmos retells the 14-year life of NASA's Opportunity rover as one long night exposure. Its real recorded route (21,089 positions from the MER Analyst's Notebook traverse table) is drawn as a light trail across NASA's orbital map of Meridiani Planum, next to NASA's own 3D model of the rover. Learners aged 12–17 follow 8 stops, from landing to the dust storm that silenced it. At each stop they see the NASA image and the evidence, and a light-paint reveal shows which part of the rover made the discovery. Every fact links to a NASA source, and everything illustrative is labelled.
details:
What it does

Opportunity was designed for 90 Martian days and drove for more than 14 years. Since June 2018 it has rested, silent, in Perseverance Valley: one of the "inactive monuments to Mars exploration" this challenge asks us to remember. Most of what a student can find about it is a static map or an article. Neither shows where a discovery happened, or which part of the rover made it.

Echoes of the Cosmos is a 5–10 minute story in the browser:

  • The journey. 8 stops in 4 chapters: Arrival, Stuck, Better water, Silence. Each stop asks a question a teenager would ask ("What happens when a rover gets stuck?"), answers it in one line, and opens a "developed print": the NASA image with its credit, the evidence, a quote, what the evidence does not tell us, 3 FAQs and the sources.
  • Tool → discovery. A light-paint reveal dims the rover and sweeps a light onto the part that did the work: the Rock Abrasion Tool, then the APXS, at Esperance (clay minerals, gentler water); the wheels at Purgatory dune; the solar arrays at the end.
  • Silence and Legacy. An illustrative dust storm, the two real dates (last position record sol 5081, last message sol 5111), then the camera rises over the whole 45 km exposure and sets "What NASA wanted to know" (from NASA's own MER science objectives) next to "What Opportunity helped reveal", each row with its source.
  • The rover, part by part (/rover): six parts of NASA's model, with what each is, how it works and what it found.
  • How this was made (/about): what is real and what is illustrative, the data method, the six gaps in the records, every credit and all 31 sources.

How it works

  • A Python ETL turns NASA's traverse table into JSON, keeping the source row order, dropping 15 exact duplicate rows, finding 6 gaps, and never inventing a position.
  • A tested replay engine moves the rover "hold-then-move" from record to record and never through a gap. Each position is labelled as recorded, between two records, or no records.
  • The route is aligned to NASA's PIA23178 map with a 2-point fit (17.67 m per pixel, 0.59°); the possible offset of up to 0.5 km is printed on screen.
  • A vanilla three.js stage draws one frame from one state (route, rover, camera, light-paint) behind a thin React text layer. The same pure function renders the 30-second film frame by frame.
  • Content (8 stops, 24 FAQs, 6 rover parts, Legacy) is stored with source IDs and checked by a lint: every source must exist and be re-opened, and phrases NASA does not use ("drinkable water", "proved life") are blocked.

Benefits and intended impact

  • The goal: a student who has never heard of Opportunity can, in about 10 minutes, retell its story from landing to silence and name at least two discoveries and the tools that made them.
  • Teachers get a ready lesson with sources they can check.
  • It shows learners how scientists know things: the evidence, its limits, and the difference between data and illustration.
  • It is open to everyone: works on phones, a Static view with the same content for low-end devices or no WebGL, a visible Reduce motion toggle, full keyboard use, and WCAG 2.2 AA (axe-core: 0 violations on 8 views at desktop and phone sizes). It works muted.

Tools, languages and hardware

TypeScript, React 19, Vite 8, three.js 0.187, Python 3 (ETL and procedural film score), Vitest and pytest, Playwright and axe-core (testing), ffmpeg (film), Vercel (hosting). Built on a laptop with an integrated GPU (Intel Iris Xe), which is also the performance target.
